mainTopic: The week of תשעה באב: does laundering to put away count, and do the restrictions continue after the fast?
overview: The amud opens with רב פפא's practical advice: a Jew with a court case against a non-Jew should avoid it in אב and pursue it in אדר. Two short teachings in the name of רב follow. One says 'a future and a hope' means palm trees and linen garments. The other says יעקב's fragrance was like an apple orchard. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's ban on haircuts and laundering in the week of תשעה באב. רב נחמן says only laundering in order to wear is forbidden, and רב ששת forbids even laundering to put away. רב נחמן survives רב המנונא's challenge from the Thursday permission, but a ברייתא refutes him. Next רב and שמואל argue over whether the restrictions continue after the fast. A ברייתא seems to refute שמואל, but he answers that תנאים disagree about this. רבי יוחנן then shows that all three תנאים learn their views from one verse in הושע, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב פפא's practical advice: avoid court cases with a non-Jew in אב, pursue them in אדר
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives practical advice based on the earlier teaching about אב and אדר. A Jew with a lawsuit against a non-Jew should avoid it in אב, when Jewish fortune is weak, and pursue it in אדר, when Jewish fortune is strong.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Therefore, a Jew who has a court case with a non-Jew should dodge him in אב, because his fortune is bad then. He should make himself available in אדר, because his fortune is good then.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא takes the earlier idea, 'reduce joy in אב, increase joy in אדר,' and turns it into practical life advice about court cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הלכך ('therefore') shows this is a consequence of what came before. If אב is a time of bad fortune for the Jewish people and אדר a time of good fortune, a Jew facing a non-Jew in court should time his case to match. The case is chosen because a lawsuit is a direct contest whose outcome depends on 'fortune.'

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore / so in practice: draws a conclusion from an earlier teaching
Fortune, luck (here, the fortune of the Jewish people)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the mourning character of אב is not only a matter of personal feelings. חז"ל treated it as a time of real vulnerability, and that affects practical decisions.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Therefore, a Jew
who has a lawsuit with a gentile,
phrases.notes: A court case against a non-Jew.

phrases.english: should avoid him in Av,
because his fortune is bad,
and he should make himself available in Adar,
because his fortune is good.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical consequence from the previous section's teaching that joy is reduced in אב and increased in אדר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Time a lawsuit against a non-Jew for אדר rather than אב, because of the people's fortune in each month.

steps.title: A future and a hope: palm trees and linen garments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another teaching of רב יהודה בריה דרב שמואל בר שילת in the name of רב. The 'future and hope' promised in ירמיהו refers to palm trees and linen garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the verse 'To give you a future and a hope,' רב יהודה the son of רב שמואל בר שילת said in the name of רב: these are palm trees and linen garments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another teaching from the same chain of rabbis it quoted just before. It is a side teaching explaining a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in ירמיהו is said to the Jews exiled in בבל. רב reads 'a future and a hope' very concretely: palm trees and linen last a long time and keep giving benefit. So God's promise includes lasting, practical blessings in exile.

keyTerms.meaning: A future and a hope (ירמיהו כט:יא)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic of halacha. The גמרא is simply collecting more teachings from the same speaker it quoted in the previous section, so don't look for a legal connection to תשעה באב.

phrases.english: "To give you a future and a hope"
phrases.notes: ירמיהו כט:יא, said to the exiles in בבל.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said
in the name of Rav:
These are palm trees and linen garments.
phrases.notes: Both last a long time and keep giving benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side collection: another teaching by the same chain of tradition that taught about אב and אדר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'A future and a hope' refers to long-lasting assets: palm trees and linen garments.

steps.title: The smell of יעקב was like an apple orchard
steps.stepSummary: A second teaching by the same chain of tradition. The 'smell of a field which ה׳ has blessed' in יצחק's blessing of יעקב is the smell of a field of apple trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the verse 'And he said: See, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field which ה׳ has blessed,' רב יהודה the son of רב שמואל בר שילת said in the name of רב: like the smell of a field of apple trees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its short list of teachings from the same speaker. This one identifies what kind of field the פסוק means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says 'a field which ה׳ has blessed,' without naming the field. רב fills in the detail: an apple orchard, known for its pleasant fragrance. This finishes the small collection before the גמרא returns to the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A field which ה׳ has blessed (בראשית כז:כז)

phrases.english: "And he said: See, the smell of my son
is like the smell of a field which the Lord has blessed"
phrases.notes: בראשית כז:כז, יצחק blessing יעקב.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said
in the name of Rav:
Like the smell of a field of apple trees.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second teaching in the same collection of statements by the same speaker.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'blessed field' of יעקב's fragrance is an apple orchard.
steps.whatToRemember: Steps 2 and 3 are a side collection of אגדה from the same chain of tradition. The real halachic discussion picks up again in the next step.

steps.title: The משנה: in the week of תשעה באב, haircutting and laundering are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: in the week in which תשעה באב falls, it is forbidden to cut hair and to launder clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The week in which תשעה באב falls: it is forbidden to cut hair and to launder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its rule. This is a setup line: the rabbis are about to argue over what exactly 'laundering' means here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'שבת' means the whole week, not just the day of שבת. The משנה forbids two things that make a person look fresh and groomed: haircuts and laundering. That week is meant to feel like mourning.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a week (not the day of שבת)

steps.confusionAlert: 'שבת שחל תשעה באב להיות בתוכה' does NOT mean 'the שבת on which תשעה באב falls.' It means 'the WEEK that contains תשעה באב.'

phrases.english: The week in which the Ninth of Av occurs
phrases.notes: Here 'שבת' means 'week.'

phrases.english: to fall within it,
it is forbidden to cut hair and to launder.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹכָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side collection of אגדה and returns to analyzing the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the week of תשעה באב, haircutting and laundering are forbidden.

steps.title: רב נחמן: only laundering in order to wear is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן limits the משנה: the ban is only on laundering clothes in order to wear them now. Laundering them to put away for later is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: They only taught this about laundering and wearing. But laundering and setting the clothes aside is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן narrows the משנה's ban on laundering. In his view, the problem is wearing freshly cleaned clothes during this sad week, not the act of washing itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא שנו אלא' signals that a rule is being limited to a narrower case. For רב נחמן, the mourning concern is how a person looks: wearing clean clothes. Washing clothes and storing them until after תשעה באב does not break the mood.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught [this rule] regarding: a formula that narrows a teaching

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
They taught [the prohibition] only for laundering and wearing,
but laundering and setting aside is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Interprets and narrows the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban is on laundering in order to wear; laundering to store is permitted.

steps.title: רב ששת: even laundering to put away is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת disagrees with רב נחמן: even laundering clothes just to put them away is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת said: Even laundering and setting the clothes aside is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא disagrees with רב נחמן and reads the משנה more strictly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב ששת, the act of laundering is itself an activity that does not fit a week of mourning, whether or not the clothes are worn. The דין now depends on which reading of the משנה is correct.

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said:
Even laundering and setting aside is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opposing view to רב נחמן's narrow reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any laundering during the week of תשעה באב is forbidden, even if the clothes will not be worn yet.

steps.title: רב ששת's proof: רב's household launderers stopped working
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת supports his view: the launderers of רב's household were idle during this week. That shows laundering itself was forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Know that this is so, because the launderers of רב's household were idle.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת brings evidence from real-life practice to prove that laundering itself is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only wearing clean clothes were forbidden, the launderers could have kept washing and the household could have stored the clothes. Their stopping work completely shows the practice was to forbid the washing itself. 'תדע' introduces this kind of supporting proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Know [that it is so]: introduces a supporting proof
Of רב's household (or: of the study hall)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: Know [that this is so],
for the launderers of Rav's household were idle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב ששת's view stated in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's view that even laundering to put away is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רב's household launderers, who stopped working during the week of תשעה באב.

steps.title: רב המנונא objects from Thursday's permission for the honor of שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא raises an objection to רב נחמן from the משנה itself: on Thursday, laundering is permitted for the honor of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא objected: On Thursday they are permitted, because of the honor of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא begins a challenge against רב נחמן. He quotes the משנה's permission to launder on Thursday, and the next step will show why this is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes an exception: on the Thursday of that week, the forbidden actions become permitted for the honor of שבת. רב המנונא will argue that this exception only makes sense if ordinary laundering, even without wearing, was forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection (from an authoritative source)

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna objected:
On Thursday they are permitted,
because of the honor of Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's narrow reading using another clause of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that laundering to set aside is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Thursday exception for the honor of שבת must be permitting something that is otherwise forbidden. As the next step shows, that only fits laundering to put away, which רב נחמן says is always permitted.

steps.title: What does the Thursday permission refer to? Not laundering to wear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of laundering the Thursday permission covers. If it means laundering to wear right away, there is no honor of שבת in wearing clean clothes on Thursday.
steps.simpleTranslation: To what does this refer? If you say laundering and wearing, what honor of שבת is there in that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens רב המנונא's objection by asking what the Thursday permission refers to. It rejects the first option, laundering to wear. The next step completes the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing clean clothes on Thursday does nothing for שבת. So the Thursday permission must be for laundering to put the clothes away for שבת. That implies laundering to put away is forbidden on the other days, which goes against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: For what? To what does it refer?
If you say: proposes a possible reading in order to test it
What ... is there?: a rhetorical challenge

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'למאי' is not a neutral side question. It is part of רב המנונא's attack, which is building toward the conclusion that the משנה forbids laundering even to put away.

phrases.english: For what [is it permitted]?
If you say: to launder and to wear,
what honor of Shabbat is there [in that]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the logic of רב המנונא's objection by testing what the Thursday permission refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of laundering does the Thursday permission refer to: laundering to wear, or laundering to put away?
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Laundering to wear on Thursday gives no honor to שבת, so the permission must be for laundering to store for שבת. That means such laundering is otherwise forbidden, which contradicts רב נחמן.
steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת is רב נחמן (only laundering to wear is forbidden) versus רב ששת (even laundering to put away is forbidden). רב המנונא is building a challenge to רב נחמן from the משנה's Thursday exception, and step 10 completes it.

steps.title: So the Thursday permission must mean laundering to put away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes רב המנונא's challenge. The Thursday permission must be about laundering to put away for שבת, which implies that putting away is forbidden the rest of the week. That contradicts רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must mean laundering to put the clothes away until שבת. And it is only on Thursday that this is permitted. But during the rest of the week, it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it started in step 9. If the Thursday permission is about laundering to put away, then laundering to put away must be forbidden on the other days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 ruled out the idea that the משנה means laundering to wear now, because that has no connection to כבוד שבת. So the permission must be about laundering to put away. But if the משנה only allows that on Thursday, then on other days it is forbidden, which is exactly what רב נחמן said was allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: To put away / set aside (for later use)

steps.confusionAlert: In this sugya, the word שבת often means 'week', not the seventh day. 'הַשַּׁבָּת כּוּלָּהּ' means 'the whole week'.

phrases.english: Rather, it must mean to put away.
phrases.notes: The only option left after step 9 ruled out 'to wear now'.

phrases.english: and it is only on Thursday that it is permitted,
but the whole week, it is forbidden!
phrases.notes: This directly contradicts רב נחמן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the either/or question of step 9 and turns it into a direct challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that laundering to put away is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Thursday permission only makes sense for laundering to put away. That implies putting away is forbidden on other days.

steps.title: The Thursday permission is about someone with only one shirt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה really does mean laundering to wear now. It is talking about someone who owns only one shirt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the משנה means laundering in order to wear the clothes now. It is talking about a person who has only one shirt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן. It says the Thursday permission is about laundering to wear now, in the special case of a person who owns only one shirt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person with only one shirt must wash it and wear it, or he will have nothing clean for שבת. So for him, washing and wearing on Thursday really is for כבוד שבת. This takes away the proof that the משנה is about putting away.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (introduces a defense of the original reading)
To launder and to wear (right away)

phrases.english: Really, it means to launder and wear,
and it refers to one who has only one shirt.
phrases.notes: With only one shirt, washing it now is the only way to have it clean for שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by redefining the case in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a person with one shirt
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Laundering to wear on Thursday has no connection to כבוד שבת, so the משנה must mean putting away.
steps.terutzMaskana: For someone with only one shirt, washing and wearing on Thursday is truly for כבוד שבת. רב נחמן stands.

steps.title: Support: a person with one shirt gets special leniency
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the one-shirt idea with רבי יוחנן's ruling: someone with only one shirt may launder it on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A person who has only one shirt is allowed to launder it on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the one-shirt case is a known reason for leniency. It quotes רבי יוחנן, who allows laundering on חול המועד for someone with only one shirt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Laundering on חול המועד is normally forbidden, yet the one-shirt person is allowed. That shows חז"ל treat this person's need as real. The same reasoning fits the Thursday permission before תשעה באב.

keyTerms.meaning: The intermediate days of a Festival

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rav Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא חָלוּק אֶחָד
phrases.english: One who has only one shirt
is permitted to launder it on the intermediate days of the Festival.
phrases.notes: This is normally forbidden on חול המועד.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 11 with a parallel ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the משנה is talking about someone with one shirt
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling about laundering on חול המועד

steps.title: רבי אלעזר agrees with רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר, who says the same thing as רב נחמן: only laundering to wear is forbidden, and laundering to put away is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי בנימין said in the name of רבי אלעזר: The ban only applies to laundering in order to wear. But laundering to put away is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another אמורא who holds exactly like רב נחמן. This adds support for רב נחמן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'איתמר נמי' tells us an independent source said the same thing. רבי אלעזר also limits the ban to laundering to wear now. So רב נחמן is not alone against רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (an independent source agreeing)
They only taught [this ruling] in the case of
רבי אלעזר, an אמורא from ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי בִּנְיָמִין אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Binyamin said in the name of Rabbi Elazar:
They taught [the ban] only for laundering and wearing,
but laundering to put away is permitted.
phrases.notes: The same view as רב נחמן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering the challenge to רב נחמן, the גמרא adds independent support for his view.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's view that laundering to put away is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר, quoted by רבי בנימין

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids laundering even to put away
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says laundering before תשעה באב is forbidden even if the clothes are put away until after the fast. It also explains which kinds of laundering count, and that linen is not subject to גיהוץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא objects: A ברייתא teaches: It is forbidden to launder before תשעה באב, even to put the clothes away until after תשעה באב. Our fine laundering (in בבל) counts like their regular laundering (in ארץ ישראל). And linen clothes are not subject to the rule of fine laundering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that directly contradicts רב נחמן and רבי אלעזר. It openly forbids laundering even just to put the clothes away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אפילו להניח' match רב ששת's view and clash head-on with רב נחמן. The rest of the ברייתא defines the ban. In בבל, only fine pressing (גיהוץ) counts as real laundering. Linen clothes do not come under גיהוץ at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a תנאי source)
Fine laundering / pressing to make clothes look new

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
It is forbidden to launder before the Ninth of Av,
even to put away until after the Ninth of Av.
phrases.notes: This is the key phrase against רב נחמן.

phrases.english: And our fine laundering is like their plain laundering.
phrases.notes: Plain washing in בבל was weak and did not count as forbidden laundering.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְלֵי פִשְׁתָּן אֵין בָּהֶם מִשּׁוּם גִּהוּץ.
phrases.english: And linen garments are not subject to fine laundering.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אָסוּר לְכַבֵּס לִפְנֵי תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the support in step 13, the גמרא brings a stronger source against that view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן and רבי אלעזר, who permit laundering to put away
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא, which carries more authority than an אמורא, explicitly forbids laundering 'even to put away'.

steps.title: רב נחמן's view is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares the ברייתא a conclusive refutation of רב נחמן's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that there is no answer to the ברייתא. רב נחמן's view, that laundering to put away is allowed, is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'תיובתא' is the strongest kind of defeat: an אמורא contradicted by a ברייתא with no way out. The law follows רב ששת, so laundering is forbidden even just to put the clothes away.
steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling: during the week of תשעה באב, laundering is forbidden even if you only plan to put the clothes away. רב נחמן's leniency is refuted, and רב ששת's view stands.

phrases.english: A refutation.
phrases.notes: Aimed at רב נחמן (and רבי אלעזר).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 14 with no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Laundering is forbidden in the week of תשעה באב even to put away, as רב ששת said.

steps.title: Linen clothes may not be worn during the week of תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that even though linen is not subject to גיהוץ, wearing freshly laundered linen during the week of תשעה באב is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר גיורי sent a message in the name of רבי יוחנן: Even though they said linen clothes are not subject to fine laundering, it is still forbidden to wear them during the week in which תשעה באב falls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the last line of the ברייתא. Linen may not count as גיהוץ, but you still may not wear laundered linen during that week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that since linen is not subject to גיהוץ, it is completely allowed. רבי יוחנן says no. Wearing fresh linen is still a sign of comfort and joy, so it is forbidden during the mourning week.

keyTerms.meaning: Sent (a ruling sent from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: Rav Yitzḥak bar Giyorei sent
in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Even though they said

phrases.aramaic: כְּלֵי פִשְׁתָּן אֵין בָּהֶם מִשּׁוּם גִּהוּץ,
phrases.english: linen garments are not subject to fine laundering,
still, it is forbidden to wear them

phrases.aramaic: בְּשַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹכָהּ.
phrases.english: during the week in which the Ninth of Av falls.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח רַב יִצְחָק בַּר גִּיּוֹרֵי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the linen clause at the end of the ברייתא in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Linen clothes are not subject to גיהוץ, yet wearing them during the week of תשעה באב is forbidden.

steps.title: רב: the restrictions apply only before the fast
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the week's restrictions apply only on the days before תשעה באב. After the fast, they are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The ban was only taught for the days before תשעה באב. After it, laundering is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens: do the week's restrictions continue after the fast day? רב says they apply only before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the restrictions apply in 'the week in which תשעה באב falls'. רב reads this to mean only the days leading up to the fast. Once the fast has passed, the mourning restrictions end.

keyTerms.meaning: רב, a leading early אמורא of בבל

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְפָנָיו,
phrases.english: Rav said: They taught [the ban] only before it,
but after it, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the time span of the restrictions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The week's restrictions apply only on the days before תשעה באב.

steps.title: שמואל: the restrictions apply even after the fast
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב. The restrictions continue even after תשעה באב, until the end of the week.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: Even after תשעה באב, it is also forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב. He holds that the restrictions last for the whole week, including the days after the fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, 'the week in which תשעה באב falls' means the entire week, both before and after the fast. So the disagreement is about how far the restriction stretches.

keyTerms.meaning: שמואל, רב's colleague and frequent disputant

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
Even after it, it is also forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ לְאַחֲרָיו נָמֵי אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing view to רב in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The restrictions apply for the whole week, even after תשעה באב.

steps.title: A ברייתא is brought to test רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא about the week of תשעה באב. It lays out how the Thursday rule works, starting with the case where the fast falls on Sunday. The ברייתא continues next.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא objects: A ברייתא teaches: In the week in which תשעה באב falls, it is forbidden to cut hair and to launder. But on Thursday these are permitted, out of honor for שבת. How does this work? If תשעה באב falls on Sunday, it is permitted to launder the entire week before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge to the רב/שמואל debate by quoting a ברייתא. This step is setting up the next move: the ברייתא's later cases (next) will make the challenge clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explains the rule case by case, depending on which day the fast falls. If it falls on Sunday, the previous week is not 'the week of תשעה באב' at all, so laundering is allowed all week. The coming cases will show whether the days after the fast are permitted, which tests שמואל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: On Sunday (the first day of the week)

steps.confusionAlert: 'כׇּל הַשַּׁבָּת כּוּלָּהּ' here means the whole week before the fast, not the day of שבת. Since the fast falls on Sunday, the previous week is not its week at all.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: שַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹכָהּ —
phrases.english: In the week in which the Ninth of Av falls,
it is forbidden to cut hair and to launder,
but on Thursday they are permitted because of the honor of Shabbat.
How so?
If it falls on Sunday,
it is permitted to launder the entire week.
phrases.notes: Meaning the whole week before the fast. The ברייתא's other cases continue next.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: שַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹכָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test the רב/שמואל debate of steps 17 and 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רב/שמואל debate about the days after תשעה באב (most likely aimed at שמואל)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's day-by-day breakdown, which continues next, will show whether the days after the fast are permitted.

steps.title: Midweek fast: forbidden before, permitted after
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if תשעה באב falls Monday through Thursday, laundering is forbidden on the days before it and permitted on the days after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If תשעה באב falls on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday, laundering is forbidden before it and permitted after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא it started in the last step. This line contains the key words that will be used against שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא clearly says 'after it — permitted.' That matches רב, who said the restrictions end with the fast. It contradicts שמואל, who said they last until the end of the week.

keyTerms.meaning: Before it (the days before the fast)
After it (the days after the fast)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not miss the importance of the short words לְאַחֲרָיו מוּתָּר ('after it, permitted'). They are the whole basis of the coming refutation of שמואל.

phrases.english: On Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday,
phrases.notes: If the Ninth of Av falls on one of these days.

phrases.english: before it — forbidden,
after it — permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא begun in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view (step 18) that the restrictions continue after תשעה באב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly permits laundering after the fast.

steps.title: Fast on Friday: laundering allowed for שבת
steps.stepSummary: If תשעה באב falls on Friday, one may launder on Thursday in honor of שבת. If he did not, he may launder on Friday from מנחה time onward.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it falls on Friday, one may launder on Thursday out of respect for שבת. If he did not launder on Thursday, he may launder on Friday from מנחה time and on.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a special case: a fast that falls on Friday, right before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally Thursday would be a forbidden day, since it comes before the fast. Here כבוד השבת overrides the rule. The ברייתא even allows laundering on the fast day itself, late in the afternoon, if Thursday was missed.

phrases.english: If it occurs on Friday —
it is permitted to launder on Thursday
because of the honor of Shabbat.
And if he did not launder on Thursday of the week —
phrases.notes: Here בשבת means 'of the week'.

phrases.english: he is permitted to launder on Friday
from מנחה time onward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the Friday case.

steps.title: אביי curses the Friday-afternoon leniency
steps.stepSummary: אביי, or some say רב אחא בר יעקב, cursed anyone who launders on the fast day itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי, and some say רב אחא בר יעקב, cursed about this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא briefly interrupts the ברייתא. It reports that an אמורא strongly rejected the last leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Laundering on the afternoon of תשעה באב itself seemed too extreme a breach of the mourning. So even though the ברייתא allows it, אביי cursed those who do it. This is a side comment, and the ברייתא resumes right after.

phrases.english: Abaye cursed concerning it,
and some say Rav Acha bar Yaakov,
on this (practice).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side comment rejecting the leniency in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Laundering on Friday afternoon of תשעה באב deserves a curse.

steps.title: Torah reading on תשעה באב by weekday
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא resumes. On Monday or Thursday, three people read and one says the הפטרה. On Tuesday or Wednesday, one reads and the same person says the הפטרה. רבי יוסי says it is always three.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it falls on Monday or Thursday, three read from the Torah and one reads the הפטרה. On Tuesday or Wednesday, one reads and that same one reads the הפטרה. רבי יוסי says: always three read, and one reads the הפטרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא, which ends with rules about the Torah reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On Monday and Thursday the Torah is read anyway, so the usual three people are called. On other days the ברייתא allows just one. רבי יוסי disagrees and requires three every time. This part is not the point of the challenge. It is quoted only because the ברייתא is being cited in full.

keyTerms.meaning: Three people read from the Torah
Reads the הפטרה (portion from the Prophets)

phrases.english: If it occurs on Monday or Thursday —
three read, and one says the הפטרה.
On Tuesday or Wednesday —
one reads, and that one says the הפטרה.
Rabbi Yosei says:
Always three read, and one says the הפטרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא resumes after אביי's interruption.

steps.title: A conclusive refutation of שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares the ברייתא a refutation of שמואל, because it permits laundering after the fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of שמואל!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא makes its point. The ברייתא (step 20) said 'after it, permitted,' which contradicts שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said the restrictions last the whole week, even after תשעה באב. The ברייתא says that after the fast laundering is permitted, so it seems to knock out שמואל completely.

phrases.english: A refutation of Shmuel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the conclusion of the challenge built from the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's words 'לְאַחֲרָיו מוּתָּר' directly contradict שמואל's ruling that the restrictions continue after the fast.

steps.title: שמואל: this is a dispute among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: שמואל can answer that תנאים argue about this. A ברייתא records רבי מאיר (ראש חודש until the fast), רבי יהודה (the whole month), and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (only that week).
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל would tell you: it is a dispute of תנאים. As it was taught: when תשעה באב falls on שבת, or the eve of תשעה באב falls on שבת, one eats and drinks all he needs and may serve a meal like שלמה's feast in his time. Haircuts and laundering are forbidden from ראש חודש until the fast; these are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: the whole month is forbidden. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: only that week is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל defends himself. The ברייתא that refuted him follows one opinion, and other תנאים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר stops the restrictions at the fast, like the ברייתא that challenged שמואל. רבי יהודה forbids the whole month, which clearly includes days after the fast. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids 'that week,' and שמואל can read that as the full week, including the days after the fast. So שמואל has תנאים on his side.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among תנאים
The feast of King שלמה (a lavish meal)

steps.confusionAlert: In this context שַׁבָּת in 'אוֹתָהּ שַׁבָּת' means 'week,' not the day of שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל is no longer refuted. His view becomes one side of a dispute among תנאים rather than a rejected opinion.

phrases.english: Shmuel could say to you:
It is a dispute of Tannaim.
As it was taught in a baraita:
The Ninth of Av that falls on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן עֶרֶב תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: and likewise the eve of the Ninth of Av that falls on Shabbat —
he eats and drinks all he needs,
and may put on his table
even a meal like Solomon's in his time.
And it is forbidden to cut hair and to launder
from Rosh Chodesh until the fast,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
The entire month is forbidden.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אָסוּר אֶלָּא אוֹתָהּ שַׁבָּת בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: It is forbidden only during that week.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute among תנאים: the challenging ברייתא reflects only one opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is the only view, so שמואל has no support and is refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Other תנאים (רבי יהודה, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל) extend the restrictions past the fast, and שמואל follows them.

steps.title: A second ברייתא with the same dispute
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא records the same three opinions about observing mourning from ראש חודש, which reinforces that this is a real dispute among תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another ברייתא teaches: one observes mourning from ראש חודש until the fast; these are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: the whole month is forbidden. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: only that week is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא to back up שמואל's claim that תנאים argue about this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא speaks of mourning practices in general, not just haircuts and laundering, but the same three positions appear. That confirms that רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל keep restrictions in place beyond the fast. שמואל can stand on their view.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's view (restrictions end at the fast) matches רבי מאיר and the ברייתא quoted in steps 19-23. שמואל's view (restrictions last the whole week) is supported by רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: And another baraita teaches:
And one observes mourning
from Rosh Chodesh until the fast,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
The entire month is forbidden.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אָסוּר אֶלָּא אוֹתָהּ שַׁבָּת בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: It is forbidden only during that week.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source to strengthen the answer in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's claim that the issue is a dispute among תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A second ברייתא with the same three-way dispute about mourning practices.

steps.title: All three opinions come from one verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the three תנאים who disagree about the mourning period all learned it from one verse in הושע: 'her festival, her new month, and her שבת.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: All three of them learned their views from one verse, as it is written: 'And I will cause all her joy to cease, her festival, her new month, and her שבת' (הושע 2:13).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains where the three-way argument from the last steps comes from. All three תנאים use the same verse but read it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we only knew that רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagree. רבי יוחנן adds that the argument is not random. Each one focuses on a different word in the verse: 'her festival,' 'her new month,' or 'her שבת' (week).

keyTerms.meaning: they explained or learned (from a verse)
her שבת (here it can also mean 'her week')

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the three time-frames (until the fast, the whole month, only that week) each match a different word in the same verse. This is the key to the next lines.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think each תנא uses a different verse. They all use the same verse. They only disagree about which word in it sets the length of the mourning period.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
And all three of them explained one verse,
phrases.notes: 'All three' means רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from step 25.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And I will cause all her joy to cease,'
phrases.notes: הושע 2:13

phrases.english: 'her festival, her new month, and her Shabbat.'
phrases.notes: Each of these three words will be linked to one of the three opinions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the verse that all three opinions in steps 25-26 come from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All three opinions about the length of the mourning period before תשעה באב come from one verse: 'her festival, her new month, and her שבת.'

steps.title: Starting to explain the first opinion: from ראש חודש until the fast
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to show how the opinion of 'from ראש חודש until the fast' (רבי מאיר) fits the verse. The explanation finishes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who said: from ראש חודש until the fast —
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא names the first opinion and is about to tell us which word of the verse it comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'the one who said' points back to רבי מאיר's view from step 25: the restrictions run from ראש חודש אב until the fast. The next line, on the next amud, will link this view to one word of the verse.

keyTerms.meaning: the one who said (refers to a known opinion)
the first day of the month (here ראש חודש אב)

phrases.english: The one who said
phrases.notes: Refers to רבי מאיר's opinion.

phrases.english: from Rosh Chodesh until the fast —
phrases.notes: The sentence is unfinished. Its end, showing which word of the verse he uses, comes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר מֵרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ וְעַד הַתַּעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins applying רבי יוחנן's verse to the first of the three opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup: the opinion 'from ראש חודש until the fast' is about to be linked to a specific word in the verse.
